Mabon joined early in 1996 and was followed within months by the current junior international Andrew Goudie. Full of enthusiasm, Mabon tells us that the Belgrave walking section from U20 above is about to see its best period in well over 10 years in the forthcoming season.
Andrew Goudie gained his Great Britain Junior Vest this year in a match in Germany and was joined by Nigel Whorlow who received his call to represent England at the end of September.

Nigel Whorlow was in a class of his own in winning the under 17 title, leading all the way. Andrew Goudie found the going tough against the winner in the under 20 age group but still managed to earn the silver medal.
U20M 10km. 5, A.Goudie 50:14.

England and Great Britain Junior International Andrew Goudie walked steadily and after seeing the likely winners disqualified, went on to take 2nd, proving that in championships, style rather than speed is the order of the day.
Racing at the same time, but in the U20M group was Andrew Goudie who gained a very respectable 3rd place to become our first member home in a race that also included the senior men and veterans.

Belgrave originally had Andrew Goudie, Nigel Whorlow, Laura Fryer, Paul Graham, Sam McNally and Stephen Whorlow Jnr (reserve) selected for the South for this match but because of other commitments such as exams and over racing, only Paul and Sam were able to accept.
